memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And when all the people saw it, they shouted for joy and fell facedown." - Lev 9:24b (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two responses at once: they shouted for joy, and they fell facedown.

Exuberance and awe. Celebration and trembling. Most of us are more comfortable with one than the other.

Some Christian traditions major on joy — noise, gladness, freedom, celebration. Others major on reverence — stillness, seriousness, the fear of the Lord. Both are drawing on something real, and both are incomplete alone.

Israel did both in the same moment.

Look at how Scripture holds them together. Serve the LORD with fear and celebrate his rule with trembling (Ps 2:11). Isaiah saw God's glory and cried, Woe to me! I am ruined! (Isa 6:5). John, seeing the risen Christ, fell at his feet as though dead (Rev 1:17) — and the same John wrote a Gospel full of joy.

Awe without joy becomes cold. Joy without awe becomes shallow.

The right response to God's glory is a heart that wants to shout and a body that wants to kneel.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Which comes more naturally to me — joy or reverence — and which do I need more of?
2. When did I last experience something of God that moved me deeply?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, give me both — joy that shouts and awe that kneels. Let me know You truly enough for both. Amen.
